BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. # Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook. Seller documents treated as untrusted counterparty material.

## Preliminary points

1. **None of the Seller's labels bind us.** The draft calls positions "negotiated", "agreed", "addressed", "settled" or "adequate". Under Playbook §0.4/§6.3, none of these is accepted without confirmation through our own authority process.
2. **The source facts are stale.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at **22 September 2026**. Today is 5 November 2026. Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay payment status and the DD-006 investigation all need a current refresh before we rely on the 22 September position in either direction.
3. **The Seller's two documents contradict each other.** The Disclosure Letter is more candid than the Seller Update and contradicts it on Bluefen, Riverlark and the funds flow. We should use the Letter's own admissions in the mark-up.

---

## Issue-by-issue review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4,800,000) (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% (AUD 6,000,000).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.**
- **Reason:** 20% is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft. None has been given, and matching a fallback number does not clear it.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, recoverable only on the excess above the basket.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Restore AUD 5k / AUD 50k on a tipping basis.**
- **Reason:** Both thresholds are five times our position, and an excess-only deductible silently removes the first AUD 250k of every recovery.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months. Any limitation also applies to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims. Separate periods for other categories.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insist on 24 months and delete the "all Claims" default.**
- **Reason:** 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval (none given). The default language is a hidden override of every other regime.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties fall under the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.**
- **Reason:** Capping title at 20% means we could pay AUD 24m for shares and recover AUD 4.8m if we do not own them. "Simplicity" is not a justification.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No express carve-out. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5). The time-limit default in cl 12.3 would also capture fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Insert an express overriding carve-out.**
- **Reason:** The drafting would purport to limit fraud claims, and the playbook says no one may waive this protection.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Letter §1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific fair disclosure only.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete §1.1–1.2. Accept only the specific disclosures, tested for fairness.**
- **Reason:** Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure shifts diligence risk to us and empties the warranties.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** The blanket exclusion deleted. Any qualifier limited to named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3.**
- **Reason:** It imputes adviser and constructive knowledge and would defeat even indemnities for matters we specifically identified, such as Ironquay.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Says the consent is "addressed". Reasonable endeavours only. Condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the written consent (cl 3/6.3).
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Make an effective consent and satisfied conditions a hard condition precedent.**
- **Reason:**
  - Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (AUD 3.6m).
  - The Seller's own Letter (§2) admits that no final consent and no evidence on the conditions has been provided, so "addressed" is unsupported.
  - Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer.
  - We should also ask for the current status as at today.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding. A release to be provided after Completion (cl 2/7).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A current payout letter.
  - Direct repayment from Completion funds.
  - Effective security releases at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the post-Completion release.**
- **Reason:** The Letter (§3) confirms the facility is unrepaid and undischarged. A post-Completion release is only possible with an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost's approval, and neither exists. We also need a refreshed balance, since AUD 3.2m is an approximate September figure.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow.
- **Buyer wants:** The AUD 420,000 plus any triggered payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Require express itemisation or deduction, with an indemnity for on-costs.**
- **Reason:** The Company is the payer. Omitting the bonuses from the funds flow silently pushes the cost onto us, and the Letter (§5) is silent on on-costs. "Agreed price mechanics" is an assertion, not an agreement.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment and is "adequate" (cl 11.1).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A broadened indemnity covering failure of SOW3 Project Materials to transfer, third-party IP claims and related loss.
  - The SOW3 cure preserved: payment plus a confirmatory assignment.
- **Recommendation:** **Broaden the indemnity. Add a pre-Completion deliverable of payment evidence and a confirmatory assignment.**
- **Reason:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. The AUD 180,000 open figure (DD-010) is unverified either way, so we should not assume it is owed or paid.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter" that is "not expected to be material".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Preservation of logs.
  - A completed investigation.
  - Regular updates before Completion.
  - Specific warranty and indemnity protection.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the materiality characterisation. Add investigation and update covenants and specific protection.**
- **Reason:** The Letter (§6) confirms that access, scope and any notification duty are undetermined for about 1,240 records. We should assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss amount in either direction, and should not accept the "not material" label either.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are "ordinary-course operating costs".
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of each renewal: whether it is unavoidable, terminable, accrued, or ordinary course. These are related renewals, so DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "ordinary course" label. Request the information. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.**
- **Reason:** The Letter (§8) itself says none of these points is established. We neither concede the Seller's position nor assert our own until the facts are in.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature". Tax and IP sit within the "general regime". Title is folded into general.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants kept as distinct categories, each with its own regime.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Delete the cross-category defaults in cl 9.3/12.3/12.8/20.5.**
- **Reason:** These are hidden general-regime overrides that collapse indemnities, covenants and payment obligations into a 20%, 18-month warranty cap.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. Examples:
  - ASIC extract.
  - PPSR search.
  - Share certificates.
  - Constitution and board approvals.
  - A no-encumbrance confirmation, including against the Riverlark security.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not rely on DD-012 alone.**
- **Reason:** The register is an internal source supplied by the Seller, and the Letter (§10) concedes it is not Buyer verification.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP are "settled" under the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP treated as OPEN, to be negotiated separately.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled". Keep both open in the mark-up.**
- **Reason:** Neither has been agreed. We should not assume a resolution or unlimited liability, and must not let the general cap absorb them by default.

---

## Other items noted (not requested)
- **Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** The Letter frames these narrowly (notification only; assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale). We should verify against the actual clauses rather than accept the Seller's characterisation.
- **Letter §1.4 (no admissions):** Acceptable as a general statement. It must not dilute specific disclosures or our specific indemnities.

## Authority status
No fallback has been authorised. Every position above that departs from our starting position, notably the 20% cap and the 18-month period, would require written approval from Amelia Frost identifying this draft before we could concede it.
